title: Gathered insights: contextuality & routing — lab notes
content:
Quick note: skimming several talks + 3 papers from ML Systems conf + followups from authors. Putting together a short list of concrete patterns that might map to Redwood Optimize experiments (low-friction). Aim: find low-effort changes that could give measurable latency/cost wins for long-context conversational workloads.

High-level takeaways (1-2 lines each):
- Contextuality is multifaceted: not just sequence length but distribution (many short edits vs single long transcript).
- Smart routing + model variants can reduce p99 latency without hurting average quality: route warm cache flows to high-quantized variants; cold flows to full-precision.
- Prefix prefetch / speculative KV warming showed ~12–20% token-latency reduction in authors' sim; needs real trace test.
- Energy-aware scheduling: batching aggressively when GPU utilisation low reduces energy-per-token — but increases tail for interactive flows.

Paper skims (notes + quick heuristics):
1) "Adaptive Prefix Prefetching for Long-Context LMs" (arXiv:2603.01234)
   - Authors: Xu et al.
   - Key idea: predict the next 2–4 tokens of prefix reuse patterns across users and pre-warm KV shards on idle GPUs.
   - Experiment: synthetic dialog traces, measured token-latency drop 12% at p50, 8% at p95.
   - My read: interesting for Redwood Dedicated where idle capacity exists. Risk: prefetch waste if prediction wrong -> small but real extra compute.
   - Quick experiment: replay 24h of prod traces with prefetcher enabled (beta) and compute net extra tokens warmed vs cache hits.

2) "Quantized Variants + Routing Policies" (conf paper)
   - Idea: keep 2 model variants per family (hq + liteq). Use a tiny classifier (10–20 tokens) on request metadata+prefix features to route.
   - Observed: cost down 30% with <1% ROC quality hit on most conv tasks.
   - Redwood mapping: leverage existing smart-routing infra to test route by user-tier and prefix-length features.

3) "Cache Eviction by Recency+SemanticScore" (workshop poster)
   - Blend recency (LRU-ish) with a cheap semantic similarity (hashed short n-gram signature) to avoid evicting semantically-similar prefixes.
   - Implementation note: hh-index of n-gram hashes can live in metadata store, not GPU.

Concrete experiments to run (priority order):
- EXP-A (trace replay): Run a prefix-prefetch simulation using 7 days of cached-prefix traces. Metrics: prefetch precision/recall, extra warmed tokens, net TTL savings (tokens avoided generating). Estimated runtime: 1 dev-day to wire trace playback into sim harness.
- EXP-B (routing prototype): Use two variants (gptx-large-8bit-lite / gptx-large-16bit-hq) and a heuristic router (prefix_len > 2048 OR user_has_session_history -> hq else lite). Measure latency/cost/quality delta on internal prompt-suite.
- EXP-C (eviction policy A/B): Replace current LRU with Recency+SemanticScore sampler (cheap n-gram hash). Measure cache hit rate and p95 lat improvement.

Operational concerns / notes:
- Telemetry: need token-level cost breakdown + per-user trace linking to see real prefetch outcomes. Add a prefetch tag to tracing spans.
- Safety: prefetching could warm prefixes that contain PII; ensure prefetch obeys privacy policy (only opaque hashed keys, no plaintext storage).
- Fallback: routing failures must have immediate fallback to hq variant with no user-visible error. Canary rollout plan spelled out below.

Canary rollout sketch for EXP-B (routing):
1) Internal dev canary: 0.5% internal tokens (dev org) for 48 hours. Monitor cost, p95, hallucination metric.
2) Beta customers: opt-in per-customer toggle in Console (Dedicated and Hosted with customer opt-in).
3) Ramp if metrics stable for 7 days. Automatic rollback on p95 latency > baseline + 20% or hallucination delta > 2% on eval set.

Notes-to-self: implementation details and cheap heuristics
- Prefetch predictor: start with a simple n-gram Markov (order 3) learned from session transcripts; complexity low.
- KV warming mechanism: extend the RPC path that populates KV shards to accept a lightweight prefetch flag that creates cache entries but marks them ephemeral (low TTL).
- Metrics calc: compute "prefetch_win_tokens" = tokens served from prefetched entries; "prefetch_waste_tokens" = prefetched entries never used before TTL. Want precision > 0.4 to proceed.

Potential pitfalls / open questions (rapid):
- How correlated are our prod traces to the synthetic traces authors used? Might overstate wins.
- Cold-start flows for new users: prefetch may be ineffective — maybe restrict to returning sessions only.
- Quantized lite variant hallucination behavior on edge-case instructions — need dedicated eval set for hallucination.

Quick sketch of an internal eval prompt set (to measure quality delta):
- 40 prompts: mix of instruction-following (20), long-context QA (10), summarization (5), code-completion (5). Each prompt executed against hq and lite variants with same seed. Compute BLEU/ROUGE+human spot checks for hallucination.

Links & references I want to re-open:
- arXiv:2603.01234 (prefetch)
- internal PR: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-prefetch-proto/pull/18 (notes + toy server)
- Console feature idea: add "routing policy audit" page (confluence:CTX-ROUTING-42)
- Slack thread: #ctx-recall ts:1700000000.000200 — short discussion with Mira about privacy constraints.

Action items (next 7 days):
- [ ] Draft a one-pager for PMC describing EXP-A and EXP-B (Ravi + me) — include rough cost model.
- [ ] Wire trace replay into the offline sim harness (ask infra for trace export, ticket INF-789).
- [ ] Build tiny router prototype in playground (proto route rules + metrics) — 2d spike.

Random heuristics to try later (brain dump):
- Warm only even-numbered shards for low-importance prefixes to reduce resource hogging.
- Evict by combining TTL + semantic novelty score (boost TTL if semantically novel).
- Region-aware routing: keep user sessions in regionally-localized low-latency pools and prefer lite variant for cross-region fallbacks.

Closing note: felt like a useful cross between paper ideas and what we can realistically ship quickly. Prioritize trace replay first — it tells us if prefetching is even promising on our workloads.

-- Leena

Notes to self: follow up with Mira on privacy constraints, set up quick sync w/ Ravi on Friday.
